newsitem.title: USA: Quaker State sees year EPS below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Quaker State sees year EPS below estimates.

text.p: Quaker State Corp said Thursday that greater than expected dilution from its recent Blue Coral acquisition is expected to push 1996 earnings per share below analysts' estimates of $0.70 to $0.75.
The dilutive effect of Blue Coral, which makes commercial car wash products, is expected to be $0.08 a share, Quaker State said.
The company previously expected the dilution to amount to $0.03 to $0.05 a share, it said.
In 1995 the company reported earnings of $0.38 a share, including a restructuring charge, on revenues of $1.04 billion.

Quaker State said its fourth quarter results would include one-time items, including a gain from the prepayment of a royalty obligation, the write-down of its West Virginia lubricants refinery, and a severance charge related to planned job cuts.
The job cuts will affect as many as 100 employees in the lubricants division but will not come at the West Virginia refinery, said Stephen Blum, senior vice president of Quaker State.
The total effect of the extraordinary items on fourth quarter results has not yet been determined, Blum said.
Quaker State said its domestic motor oil business is on track to show an eight percent volume increase over last year. It said it expects continued improvement during 1997.
The company said it anticipates "significant synergies" from the consolidation of Slick 50, Blue Coral and its Medo car products operations.
